newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber trade thin ahead of Easter break.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber trade thin ahead of Easter break.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was thin on Thursday although some players expect the market to perk up ahead of the Easter holdiays, dealers said.
"It's really, really thin. There are just no orders and Japan is also providing us with no leads this morning," a dealer for a foreign rubber brokerage house said.
"There's really nothing going on right now. I would like to think though that there should be more activity this afternoon," a dealer for a North American trading house said.
The trade was unmoved by news that the Thai government recently bought 7,000 tonnes of rubber.

"You have to ask yourself how long they can keep this kind of subsidy up," another dealer said. Some small-lot buying was seen for RSS3 grade rubber, but there was little else by way of action in the market.

At around 0945 GMT, May RSS3 was indicated unchanged at 121.00 U.S. cents a kg. May RSS1 was indicated steady at 175.00 Singapore cents (US$1.22) a kg. May TSR20 was indicated at 161.50 Singapore cents (US$1.13) a kg from 162.50 cents.
